text: Lakeflow's declarative model and a traditional notebook pipeline reach the same destination. Here's the honest trade-off between them, both directions.
Once you've declared the tables, Lakeflow retries a failed update on its own, tracks which rows a streaming table has already processed, and runs every table in the correct inferred order.
A traditional notebook pipeline reaches the same destination, but retries, checkpoint management, and task chaining are all your job to write and maintain by hand.
A traditional notebook is fully yours to debug cell by cell, mid-run. A Lakeflow pipeline runs as a whole graph — a real adjustment to how debugging works, not a downgrade.
A one-off script or a team still learning PySpark: keep the notebook. Real production SLAs and years of maintenance ahead: Lakeflow's automation starts paying for itself.
